title: What-If Tool — Check-in kiosk logs tutorial

say.5,764: five thousand, seven hundred and sixty-four

scenes.title: Check-in kiosk logs
scenes.subtitle: See where drivers spend their time at check-in
scenes.narration: This tutorial shows how to read the check-in kiosk logs in the What-If Tool: where drivers spend their time, and how the AI assistant can help.

scenes.title: From raw kiosk events to driver visits
points: 5,764 raw events from kiosk LT 010, logged in German
Every step in English, with its phase and time
scenes.narration: Before entering the yard, every driver checks in at a self-service kiosk, which logs each screen as a German status message. The tool groups 5,764 of those messages into 34 driver visits, translates every step into English, and measures how long each screen takes.

scenes.caption: Plain-English summary
scenes.narration: Start with the plain-English summary at the top. It is written straight from the data, with no AI involved. A typical visit takes two minutes 25 seconds, and 8 of the 34 visits never reached the closing screen.

scenes.caption: Key numbers
scenes.narration: Below it, five key numbers give the scale: 34 visits, 5,764 events, the typical visit length with its slow tail, events per visit, and 21 different screens.

scenes.caption: Time per step

highlights.label: Hover for the German name and both times

scenes.narration: The time per step chart ranks the slowest screens. The solid bar is the typical time, and the faded bar is the slow tail. Choosing a language normally takes 41 seconds, but the slowest visits stay on it for almost 40 minutes. Hover over a bar to see the German screen name and both times.

scenes.caption: One driver’s visit

highlights.label: Where did the time go? Setup: 97 %

scenes.narration: Click a visit in the sessions table to open it. Visit 1420 took 41 minutes. The bar at the top, Where did the time go, shows that 97 percent went into setup, almost all of it on the language screen. Names and signatures stay masked unless you click Reveal P I I.

scenes.caption: Every step in detail
scenes.narration: Every step is listed with its English name and the German kiosk name underneath. Click a step to expand it. You see its phase, whether it is a screen the driver uses, the exact start and end times, and the raw kiosk messages.

scenes.title: Ask why a screen is slow
scenes.question: Which dialog has the longest tail, and what could explain it?
scenes.note: Runs on phi4, a local model: the logs stay on your machine.
scenes.narration: The round button in the bottom-right corner opens the AI assistant, which runs locally on your machine. We asked which screen has the longest tail. It named the language screen, quoted the real figures, and suggested causes, such as drivers being unsure which language to pick.

scenes.title: Ask about the open visit
scenes.question: Is there anything unusual about the session I have open? Did the driver finish?
scenes.note: Its reasons are ideas to check. Verify its numbers on the page.
scenes.narration: It also reads the visit you have open. For visit 1420, it confirmed the driver finished, and pointed to the 39 minutes spent in setup. Treat its reasons as ideas, and check its numbers against the page.

scenes.title: Four good habits
points: Look for long faded bars in the chart
Check what the AI says against the page
scenes.narration: To recap. Start with the plain-English summary. Look for long faded bars in the time per step chart. Keep personal data masked unless you need it. And check what the AI says against the page.
